races.title: State Senate, District 10
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jesse Battles

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Small business owner and seventh-generation Etowah County native from Attalla. Studied at Gadsden State Community College and Jacksonville State University. Worked in the Alabama Secretary of State's office. Past president of the Gadsden Rotary Club. Independent candidate for State Senate District 10 in 2026.

controversies.text: In February 2026 the Alabama Republican Party's steering committee removed Battles from the Republican primary ballot. A challenge said he broke party rules by doing paid political work in 2018 for an independent who ran against a Republican. Battles says the party misapplied its own six-year rule. He then qualified as an Independent.

cands.gaps: We could not find his birth date or his birthplace beyond his campaign site's description of him as an Etowah County native. We also could not find where he grew up, the name or type of his business, or exact dates for his Secretary of State's office job. His site mentions economic-development board service and helping secure the Minth Group investment, but we found no independent confirmation. We found no public record of him holding elected office or sponsoring bills. We found no documented stances on data centers, and no stated positions on homestead taxes, restrictions on foreign or investor land purchases, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no news coverage or official finding explaining why he was removed from the Republican ballot. We found no endorsements. Ballotpedia says he did not complete its candidate survey.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he is pro-life and will stand for the right to life. He also promises support for pregnancy resource centers, rural healthcare, adoption and working families.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says that, as an NRA member and gun owner, he will oppose state or federal efforts to erode Second Amendment protections and will block mandates and invasive registries.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site pledges to support law enforcement and to protect municipal law enforcement resources.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he will protect the district's rivers, parks and natural lands so the outdoor heritage is preserved for future generations. It does not mention growth limits.

cands.name: Andrew Jones

money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.
money.source: Alabama Fair Campaign Practices Act system, downloaded Nov 5, 2026

cands.bio: Republican state senator for Alabama Senate District 10 since 2018. Founded Deep South Coffee Factory in Centre in 2017, is a fourth-generation farmer, and holds a Master of Public Policy from William & Mary and a music degree from Berea College.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Andrew Jones was born or when he came to Alabama; only his hometown of Centre is stated. We found no documented position from him on data centers or on large development projects. His campaign site mentions protecting the Coosa River waterways, but gives no specific actions on growth or land. We found no stated position on immigration or H-1B, school choice or vouchers, or red flag laws and other gun measures. We found nothing on police pay or pensions. We found no reported controversies or notable endorsements. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. The campaign site's education section was cut off, so what it says about school policy was not read in full. Claims on his campaign site about past votes are his own statements and were not checked against outside records.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site calls Centre, AL his hometown, says his family has farmed in the area for four generations, and says he was active in the Cherokee County Republican Party since high school; his birthplace is not stated in the pages reviewed. · Money: 6% of money from District 10 ZIP codes

qual.background: Alabama state senator since November 2018 (re-elected 2022), Master of Public Policy, founder of a coffee roasting business since 2017, and a family farm shareholder.
qual.why: Nearly eight years of prior legislative service plus a public policy degree and business ownership put him in the high range; committee roles were not counted.

land-for-floridians.evidence: His campaign site says he has supported legislation to prevent foreign adversaries such as China, Iran, North Korea and Russia from buying Alabama farmland. No bill number or record was given on the page.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he voted to cap and restrict property tax increases that can hit farmers hardest, and describes his approach as small government and low taxes. The specific vote is not identified on the page.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he believes in preserving the sanctity of life and has sponsored multiple bills to promote adoption.
